question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Under the weather

options.text: Late to reach due to bad weather
Surrounded by serious problems of job

solution:
The correct answer is **"Minor sickness".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"under the weather"** means to be slightly unwell or in low spirits. (थोड़ा अस्वस्थ होना)

 
 
• **Example**: *I decided not to go to school as I was feeling a little under the weather.*
 
 
 
• Thus, we can conclude that **"Minor sickness"** which refers to a mild or not very serious illness is the correct meaning of the idiom **"Under the weather."**
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **"Minor sickness".**

Therefore, the correct answer is** "Option 3".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raining heavily**: It refers to a significant amount of precipitation falling from the sky in the form of raindrops, typically at a fast rate. (मूसलाधार वर्षा)
 
• **Late to reach due to bad weather**: It indicates that someone or something arrived at its destination later than expected because of adverse weather conditions. (खराब मौसम के कारण पहुंचने में देर)
 
• **Surrounded by serious problems of job**: It implies that someone is facing significant difficulties or challenges related to their employment or occupation. (नौकरी की गंभीर समस्याओं से घिरे होना)
